**My reasoning as this farmer:**

I have been farming this land since I was young, same as my father before me. Here in Quzhou, everyone grows wheat in winter and corn in summer. That is what the land here is good for. I have about 10 mu — I manage it myself with my wife, though my back is not as strong as it used to be.

I do not overthink these things. I plant winter wheat in October after the summer corn comes off, and I plant corn in June after the wheat is cut. Same rotation I have done for thirty years. My neighbors do the same.

For wheat, I use the improved seed the village supply co-op sells — I don't know the variety name well but it has been reliable. For corn, I buy hybrid seed, also from the co-op. The hybrid corn gives more yield. Even I can see that.

For fertilizer, I put on what my father taught me, maybe a little more now because the soil feels poorer than it used to. I apply the fertilizer in two rounds — base fertilizer before planting, and top dressing when the plants are growing. I irrigate from the well. Wheat needs water four times at least — once before winter, once in spring when it greens up, once when the stalk stretches, once when it heads. Corn I water less, maybe twice.

I spray herbicide in spring for the wheat, and I watch for aphids. For corn I spray once for pests. That is usually enough.
